headline: Athletics federation bans two athletes from women's events, strips medals
summary: Jannat Begum and Kabita Roy are permanently banned after medical tests found they had Differences of Sex Development (DSD) and exceeded testosterone limits.
details: The Bangladesh Athletics Federation has permanently banned athletes Jannat Begum and Kabita Roy from competing in the women's category. The federation also cancelled all medals and national records they had previously won.

The decision followed medical examinations by a five-member expert board from Bangladesh Medical University. The board found both athletes had 46,XY Differences of Sex Development (DSD) and testosterone levels far exceeding the World Athletics limit of 2.5 nmol/L.

Jannat Begum, 28, recorded a testosterone level of 19.66 nmol/L, while 19-year-old Kabita Roy recorded 16.50 nmol/L. Under regulations, athletes must maintain levels below 2.5 nmol/L for 24 months to compete as women.

As a result, Jannat has been stripped of eight gold, one silver, and two bronze medals, including two national records in javelin and discus throws. Kabita has lost one gold, one silver, and two bronze medals from sprinting events.
The federation stated that the medals will be redistributed to the athletes who finished in the next positions. The decision was taken unanimously by the federation's Executive Committee on Saturday.
While the federation has ruled them ineligible to compete as female athletes, the Bangladesh Olympic Association secretary general noted that the athletes could still challenge the decision.
caption:

As a result, Jannat has been stripped of eight gold, one silver, and two bronze medals, including two national records in javelin and discus throws. Kabita has lost one gold, one silver, and two bronze medals from sprinting events.

The federation stated that the medals will be redistributed to the athletes who finished in the next positions. The decision was taken unanimously by the federation's Executive Committee on Saturday.

headline: History within reach as Bangladesh corner Australia in Darwin Test
summary: The Tigers have reduced Australia to 161/4 on day three, putting themselves in a strong position to secure one of their biggest Test wins ever.
details: Bangladesh tightened their grip on the Darwin Test on Saturday, putting themselves in a strong position to secure one of the biggest wins in their Test history.
After taking a 228-run first-innings lead, the Tigers reduced Australia to 161 for four at stumps on day three, leaving the hosts 67 runs ahead with two days remaining.
Earlier in the day, Bangladesh extended their first innings total to 426, thanks to a crucial 65 from Mehidy Hasan Miraz and support from the lower order.

caption:
A historic victory is within reach! 🇧🇩

Bangladesh has Australia on the ropes in the Darwin Test.

Bangladesh tightened their grip on the Darwin Test on Saturday, putting themselves in a strong position to secure one of the biggest wins in their Test history.

After taking a 228-run first-innings lead, the Tigers reduced Australia to 161 for four at stumps on day three, leaving the hosts 67 runs ahead with two days remaining.

Earlier in the day, Bangladesh extended their first innings total to 426, thanks to a crucial 65 from Mehidy Hasan Miraz and support from the lower order.

Mehidy's all-round performance was pivotal, as he not only contributed with the bat but also removed Steve Smith for 44 to maintain pressure on the hosts.

Australia remains confident of a comeback, with Josh Hazlewood noting the disciplined bowling of the Tigers while celebrating his own milestone of 300 Test wickets.

With two days left, Bangladesh now has the chance to achieve a historic upset against a full-strength Australian side in their own backyard.
